title: Application of machine learning for identification of heterotic groups in sunflower through combined approach of phenotyping, genotyping and protein profiling.
summary: The primary study applies unsupervised ML to combined phenotype, marker-genotype and protein profiles from 109 sunflower genotypes to identify heterotic groups. It supports a specific breeding-analysis result, but does not show that the groupings improved hybrid yield. Testing: The primary study applies unsupervised ML to combined phenotype, marker-genotype and protein profiles from 109 sunflower genotypes to identify heterotic groups. It supports a specific breeding-analysis result, but does not show that the groupings improved hybrid yield.. Primary full-text PDF/PMC report identifies three clustering methods applied to 109 sunflower genotypes, forms 12 heterotic groups and evaluates selected crosses; the evidence supports a breeding-analysis result, not proven yield gains.
